reason: Proposes an agent-based population algorithm to generate the synthetic instances of the over-sampling step in a stream ensemble; own algorithm, no named resampling comparison.
New Imbalanced Triangle Synthetic Data oversampler that generates in triangles instead of line segments, compared with SMOTE and its variants.
PPEO: new prototype clustering, new spatially deterministic oversampler and evolutionary search of the resampling strategy; the 14 comparators are not said to be resamplers.
Augmentation pipeline of masking plus image rotations and Gaussian-process resampling with redshifting of light curves; standard generators without a stated change, only before/after comparison.
C3GNN contribution is clustering plus contrastive graph learning; synthetic samples come from standard Mixup used as is, compared only with unnamed baselines.
FDCTGAN is a standard CTGAN trained locally on each federated client, no change to the generator; compared with Local SMOTE-FL and centralized CTGAN.
New perceptual-borderline oversampling and Perceptual Borderline SMOTE defined in arousal-valence space, compared with random oversampling and SMOTE.
Boundary-Boost synthesizes from boundary positives inside boosting and deletes misclassified synthetic samples; parts not shown to be standard, no named comparison.
O2PF is a new oversampler based on unsupervised optimum-path forest, compared with three well-established oversampling methods.
HCBOU is a new hybrid cluster-based over- and undersampling scheme for multiclass data; comparators are unnamed state-of-the-art algorithms.
New evidential hybrid resampling that uses evidence-theory soft labels to select instances for multiclass under- and oversampling, compared with other resampling methods.
PSO searches the oversampling percentage per class for SMOTE on PCA-reduced hyperspectral data, a search for how much to oversample; no resampling comparison.
New distance-based probabilistic oversampler that models the minority distribution and borderline geometry, compared with statistical and structural oversamplers.
Hierarchical synthesis chains SMOTE with a standard WGAN-GP trained on hard boundary samples; no stated change to the generator, so B2 applies despite comparison with SMOTE.
TargetShift ranks and selects the output of unchanged existing tabular generators, a separate filter after a standard generator; compared with SMOTE, CTGAN, TabDDPM, TabSyn.
EC-WCGAN pairs a standard Wasserstein conditional GAN with an external classifier; no stated change to the generator, compared with ADASYN.
VOS is presented as a new VAE-based oversampling technique whose change is not described, coded as a newly named oversampler; compared with traditional oversampling.
ConvGeN is a new deep generative model learning convex-combination coefficients of minority samples, compared with deep generative and interpolation oversamplers.
Authors adapt their own bicriterion oversampler to multiclass data with OVO and AdaBoost, a multiclass scheme of its own; compared with state-of-the-art balancing algorithms.
Time-conditioned conditional GAN generates horizon-specific minority loans, read as a new conditioning; compared with oversampling baselines, though main gain is from the graph model.
SSAS is a new adaptive synthetic sampler interpolating in a spectral-spatial neighborhood, part of the SSFRoS ensemble; compared with unnamed baselines.
Adversarial Oversampling is a new name for a standard InfoGAN generating heartbeat images before a CNN; compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and random oversampling.
GPrUS2M is a SMOTE variant whose neighbor sets are chosen by a new grouped probabilistic update optimizer within an intrusion-detection framework; no resampling comparison.
SASMOTE applies standard SMOTE to features from a new self-attention encoder-decoder, an existing sampler in a learned space; no comparison with other resampling.
MECS-Ensemble does per-cluster under- and oversampling in manifold space with an evolutionary search over optional existing operations; compared only with other imbalance learning methods.
SDSF-EGAN changes the GAN: noise sampled from an estimated minority distribution, a minority residual in the discriminator loss and a reshaper; no named resampling comparison.
Loyalty-SMOTE adds a new Loyalty criterion for noise and boundary detection and Loyalty-based denoising around SMOTE; comparators are only 'different algorithms'.
CBOUS is a newly named clustering-based over- and undersampling technique whose parts are not shown to be standard; compared only with unnamed existing techniques.
DOSMOTE optimises SMOTE synthetic samples with Darwinian PSO for multimajority multiclass data, compared with conventional oversampling strategies.
New virtual sample generation around minority support vectors under a smoothness hypothesis; only shown effective, no resampling comparison.
C-MIEN relabels clusters to reduce the number of classes before over- and undersampling and ensembling, a multiclass resampling scheme of its own; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
DTO-SMOTE generates examples in a Delaunay tessellation mesh of simplices, compared with Geometric-SMOTE, SVM-SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE and SMOTE.
SMOTE-M is the authors' own modified SMOTE whose change is not described, compared with SMOTE, ADASYN and SMOTE-Adaboost.
Affinity-propagation clustering then SMOTE per cluster with exemplars as the basis, a clustering-then-SMOTE chain of standard parts; no resampling comparison.
Undersampling plus GPT-4o-mini review generation prompted with mutual-information representative words; the language model is used unchanged, so B2 applies.
Dynamic Seasonal SMOTE is introduced as a novel SMOTE variant whose change is not described, within a water-quality system; no resampling comparison.
Gaussian-based SMOTE changes SMOTE generation with a Gaussian distribution; only shown to work on real cases, no comparison named.
New multiclass oversampler that selects minority samples by information entropy and synthesizes after PCA decorrelation; validated without named comparison.
Pipeline integrates samples from an unchanged diffusion model with selection and a fixed partial balancing policy; standard generator, compared with real-only training.
Contribution is a dynamic ensemble with drift detector for streams; an unnamed adaptive oversampler with a KNN overlap check is one step, not shown to be new.
HiOC sets the rate by Cohen's criterion, adds progressive fuzzy-information oversampling and a Mahalanobis-distance GAN per cluster; compared only with existing algorithms.
SPD Gaussian-SMOTE adapts Gaussian SMOTE synthesis to the Riemannian SPD manifold; compared only with unnamed existing methods.
DB-SVM cleaning, standard SMOTE and a confidence score on each synthetic point before classification, a chain with a post-generation screen; compared only with classifiers.
FCMSMT chains fuzzy C-means with SMOTE and undersampling to the mean class size, standard parts; compared only across classifiers.
TDCGAN is a new GAN architecture with one generator, three discriminators and an election layer, compared with traditional oversampling techniques.
OCSK-SMOTE removes outliers with one-class SVM then applies SMOTE in minority-rich K-means clusters, a chain of standard parts; tested without comparison.
Genetic Beta Oversampling is a new genetic oversampler encoding a recall-precision preference, compared with SMOTE and SMOTE-IPF.
IMGAN-MO adds a Wasserstein inter-class separation term to the GAN objective plus multiratio oversampling, compared with classical and deep generative oversamplers.
KM-SMOTE is K-means clustering of the minority class then standard SMOTE per cluster, presented as the method and compared with SMOTE.
New supervised over-sampling algorithm for binding-residue prediction whose change is not described; only shown to help, no named comparison.
Skipped Moving Average is a new oversampling technique for video time series, compared with SMOTE.
New hybrid sampling with principal-curve confidence regions for over- and undersampling plus synthetic sample selection in online ELM; compared with OS-ELM using SMOTE.
ReCO-BGA targets genetic-based oversampling at instances a three-class bagging model predicts as overlap, read as a new way of applying oversampling; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
BIDC1 and BIDC2 are newly named diversity oversamplers using an ELM autoencoder and a GAN, change not detailed; the 14 comparators are not said to be resamplers.
DTW-SMOTE changes SMOTE's similarity to dynamic time warping for time series; only before/after comparison.
Three-stage generation chains SMOTE, a GAN and a VAE with no stated change to the generators; compared with GAN-, CWGAN-, SMOTE- and VAE-based pipelines.
Standard SeqGAN generates minority log messages before autoencoder features and a GRU; no change to the generator, only before/after.
New adversarial contrastive training of the generator's latent space and prototype-based compensation of poor generations; no named comparison.
New relabeling augmentation that reuses matched beacon signals from majority locations for minority locations, compared with random oversampling, SMOTE and ADASYN.
New counterfactual oversampler perturbing near-boundary majority samples until an SVM labels them minority; compared with state-of-the-art balancing techniques.
New mixture copula with discrete margins estimated by Bayesian sampling, used to oversample; compared only with unnamed benchmark methods.
The 'novel' oversampler is described only as a GAN trained to mimic minority samples, a standard generator; compared with SMOTE, ROS, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE.
Nia-GNNs proposes a new node interpolation selecting nodes by predicted label and similarity with class-wise ratios and neighbor insertion; no named comparison.
OS-YATSI combines the YATSI semi-supervised method with an unspecified oversampling strategy for severity ranking; no new sampler shown, compared only with classifiers.
HeteAUG fuses interpolation and convolutional GAN samples and adds its own constrained heuristic search for problem-space samples; compared with other augmentation models.
EWGAN conditions the WGAN on a new entropy-weighted label vector, a new conditioning; compared with other oversampling algorithms.
IMOC iteratively selects hardest minority instances and samples from an ordinal-aware weighted distribution, with ensembles; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
Diversity oversampling with a modified D2GAN, compared with SMOTE-related and GAN-related approaches.
SMO splits samples into common and unique subspace parts, oversamples and generates them separately and restores them; compared with classical and new oversamplers.
BSCGAN is a conditional GAN with a new behavioral-sequence LSTM discriminator; only before/after improvement reported.
GK-SMOTE extends SMOTE with Gaussian KDE to separate safe and noisy regions, compared with state-of-the-art oversampling techniques.
FOST is a newly named over-sampling technique whose change is not described; compared only with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
DB-QCS and KM-QCS add a quadrilateral-centroid SMOTE that limits the synthesis area after clustering-based undersampling; compared with SMOTE.
OOLASVM combines active selection with oversampling of support vectors in online learning, compared with oversampling-based online learners.
AESMOTE introduces an adapted SMOTE, change not described, inside adversarial reinforcement learning; compared with SMOTE, ROS and NearMiss.
Proposes a novel ACGAN with an added attention mechanism for attack traffic, a stated architecture change; compared with SMOTE.
SCIF-CFGRF is a new rectified-flow generator with new blocks, loss and guidance sampler; compared with a DDPM-based model and mainstream generators.
K-means cluster-based oversampling with no further detail names only standard parts; compared with existing oversampling algorithms.
SDA-OS is a new oversampler with compressed-sensing density estimation, adaptive neighborhoods and a Beta-weighted synthesizer, compared with other oversampling techniques.
RASyn is a new adaptive synthetic sampler with interpolation direction selection and location restriction; compared only with plain stacking.
WSMOTE-ensemble hybridizes the existing weighted SMOTE with bagging over sampling composite mixtures, SMOTE inside an existing ensemble; no other resampling named as compared.
Generative oversampler with von Mises-Fisher class latents, a new distance-minimization loss and boundary latent sampling; no named comparison.
ASMC-GMO extends Gaussian-mixture oversampling with adaptive particle filtering, split-merge evolution and sparsity-preserving generation for recommender interactions; no named comparison.
CHSMOTE selects border minority seeds and defines a convex-hull synthesis area, a new SMOTE variant; no named comparison.
A novel Dual-Balanced SMOTE strategy balancing class and gender is one preprocessing step of a stacking ensemble whose contribution lies elsewhere; coded own as a newly named SMOTE strategy.
SDMA generates minority images dynamically per self-paced batch according to class performance, a new allocation, and filters low-similarity samples; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
New oversampler using real-value negative selection to generate minority data; experiments contrast it with existing over-sampling methods.
WBSWK clusters with WK-means and oversamples clusters with weights by imbalance ratio, then undersamples, read as a new per-cluster allocation; comparators are unnamed 'other methods'.
Hybrid method creating minority samples with fuzzy logic then CHC evolutionary undersampling, a new generator; over-sampling rate compared with other methods.
Oversampling with an 'improved' ACGAN whose change is not described, alongside the TIBS detector; compared only with traditional methods.
SMOTE k-out generates synthetic samples outside the local neighbourhood, a new SMOTE variant; no comparator named.
New oversampler that weights minority instances by instance hardness and samples from fitted multivariate Gaussians, compared with other oversamplers.
Adds edge constraints to SinDiffusion generation of rare-class images, a constrained generative model; only shown effective.
New conditional generative adversarial capsule network architecture, compared with general data-increasing methods.
Combines under- and oversampling based on association rules and a GAN with no stated change to either; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
COVIDDCGAN modifies DCGAN with a Haar-transform pooling layer, compared with the standard DCGAN.
DDHS learns a class-separable embedding with new losses and selects samples by density for hybrid sampling in that space; comparators are unnamed methods.
New borderline majority undersampling plus chaos-based minority beat oversampling; compared only with published classifier architectures.
MCMCRO joins MCMC with random oversampling and GANMCMCRO puts it in the GAN generator, new algorithms; only the two are evaluated.
No abstract; the title announces an improved neighborhood-KDE oversampling method, so a new method is suggested but cannot be checked.
MFSMOTE is a new multi-fidelity SMOTE where low-fidelity data guide high-fidelity data, compared with 12 oversampling algorithms.
TWKO splits k-means++ clusters into three-way domains with a balance exponent and uses distinct sampling per domain, a new allocation; benchmarks not said to be resamplers.
SC-CTGAN combines spectral clustering with a CTGAN that has no stated change; compared only with machine learning models.
A CGAN-based model generating money-laundering graph patterns that keep connectivity; the abstract does not say whether the CGAN itself is changed. Compared with SMOTE and ADASYN.
FRSSA is a new density-based regional synthetic sampler and ASST optimises the augmentation ratios; only split strategies are compared.
SPVL is a new structure-preserving variational encoder-decoder architecture that generates minority samples in its latent space; compared with state-of-the-art oversampling counterparts.
FraudDiffuse modifies diffusion with a non-fraud prior and a contrastive loss, compared with SMOTE, GANs and vanilla diffusion.
Parallel MapReduce implementation of the existing NRSBoundary-SMOTE for efficiency, no stated change to the sampling; no other resampling compared.
Incremental-SMOTE is a newly named oversampler whose change is not described, compared with SMOTE, safe-level and borderline SMOTE.
The 'improved SMOTE' is DBSCAN clustering then SMOTE within clusters, a clustering-then-SMOTE chain; no resampling comparison.
MMMmOT is a new oversampler using minority-majority mix means to generate samples, compared with traditional oversampling techniques.
Over- and undersampling integrated into a boosting framework, resampling inside an existing ensemble with no new sampler; compared with SMOTE among others.
SGO-CL fine-tunes a conditional WGAN-GP incrementally with EWC regularization, a stated training change; compared with SMOTE and generative baselines.
Two-phase oversampling chains SMOTE with a CGAN that refines SMOTE samples, no stated change to the CGAN; compared only with classifiers.
Enhanced GAN with a U-net generator from modified normal samples and discriminator features in the generator loss; no named comparison.
QGOPQC is a new quantum generative oversampler built on parameterized quantum circuits, compared with SMOTE.
A modified SMOTE designed by the paper, change not described, paired with SVM; compared only with standard SVM.
Improved D2GAN adds positive-class information to generator and discriminator and a classifier; only shown to improve classification.
Four-step methodology of successive standard SMOTE applications, a chain of existing steps; compared with undersampling and hybrid approaches.
Designs a Gaussian-mapping-enhanced G-SMOTE that adjusts boundary weights, used with AdaBoost-TWSVM; compared with SMOTE and undersampling.
New oversampling that applies SMOTE only to a selected portion of the data, a new way of applying SMOTE; no comparison named.
A plain GAN is trained to mimic minority fraud examples; compared only with training on original data.
NBCDO is a new cluster-based diversity oversampler using neighbourhood clustering and NOAH diversity optimisation, compared with DB-SMOTE, MAHAKIL, k-means SMOTE.
SMOTE-AAE-RF is SMOTE followed by an adversarial autoencoder used as a filter and a random forest; compared with unnamed competitor methods.
COUSS uses a TCP slow-start rule to decide how much to oversample, a search for the amount; compared with SMOTE, borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN and GAN oversampling.
AMR allocates synthetic minority samples by local density, overlap and variability and uses constrained interpolation; compared with SMOTE-ENN and hybrid methods.
3WOS uses three-way density clustering to find fringe regions and interpolates in purified regions, a new oversampler; no named comparison.
AMulSys proposes a category-prior-guided Mixup extended to multimodal graph representations with labels biased to the abnormal class, a stated change; compared with unnamed approaches.
IDBMORate is a new algorithm for calculating oversampling rates for binary and multiclass data, a way of deciding how much to oversample; generator not named, no comparison.
COS-HMM trains a standard HMM on the corpus and samples it as a document generator, no stated change to the model; compared with ROS and SMOTE.
GAPBoost generates triangle centre-of-gravity samples within minority K-means clusters, then prunes noise and boosts; compared only with ensemble algorithms.
DB-SLSMOTE is DBSCAN clustering of the minority class then standard Safe-Level-SMOTE per cluster, a chain of existing parts; no resampling comparison.
Integrates hybrid under- and oversampling strategies, not named or changed, inside an ensemble classifier; no resampling comparison named.
NSS adds a triple-weight allocation of synthetic samples per FCM cluster and a switching Gaussian/uniform oversampler after imputation; comparators not said to be resamplers.
New streaming oversampling driven by current class ratios and per-class errors, with active learning; compared only with stream ensembles.
AROSS finds representative minority areas by optimised clustering and samples from truncated hyperspherical Gaussians; no named comparison.
MGSN's contribution is granularity learning; its NUA module combines resampling with standard sample augmentation, no stated new generator.
ANVO is a new average-neighbor-vector extension of SMOTE, compared with state-of-the-art data augmentation techniques.
Image-to-image translation GAN used as is to synthesize plant disease images; results compared across classes only.
Novel weighted SMOTE generating weighted synthetic instances each round of transfer AdaBoost; compared with boosting-family algorithms.
MIOSDS is a newly named stream oversampling technique with multimodal filtering, change not described; no comparison named.
ANS adapts the number of SMOTE neighbors per region and adds 1NN handling of minority outcasts; no comparator named.
Generates positives uniformly within each instance's enemy-nearest-neighbor hypersphere with MapReduce before an ELM fuzzy-integral ensemble; compared with SMOTE and SMOTE+RF-BigData.
Presents SMOTEBagging as a novel improvement of SMOTE for multiclass ensembles; compared with under-sampling, over-sampling and SMOTE in the ensemble.
Gaussian oversampling with a sparse Ledoit-Wolf inverse covariance for high dimensions, read as a stated change to fitting; compared with popular competitors.
Genetic algorithm with a regression fitness model searches the per-class SMOTE ratios, a search for how much to oversample; compared only with the original data.
An enhanced TimeGAN that omits selected gradients is one component of a transformer and TRPO threat-detection framework; compared only with transformer baselines.
KFCM-KSMOTE-SVM chains kernel FCM and SMOTE applied in kernel space with an SVM, existing parts; compared only with other prediction models.
Learns an iterative minority-majority mix-up policy via an MDP and actor-critic, a new way of generating samples; no named comparison.
Copula joint distribution sampled by Monte Carlo and labeled by the rockburst grading standard, a standard generator with no stated change; compared with SMOTE.
Hybrid method with noise removal, kernel fuzzy clustering, alpha-cut majority reduction and a firefly-based SMOTE in minority clusters; compared with 20 data-level methods.
GVA adds visibility neighbor filtering, Voronoi boundary constraints and density-adaptive directional filling to SMOTE; compared with data generation baselines.
GIE-GAN initialises the generator with a VAE and adds an independent classifier to GAN training; compared with rival generative oversamplers.
Uses a class-conditional DDPM for minority time series with no stated change to the diffusion model; compared with augmentation techniques.
GraphST synthesizes minority nodes with a new path-diversity sampler, gated majority-minority fusion and neighbor generator; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
WSMOTEBoost weights SMOTE seed sampling by distance and AdaBoost weights with cost-sensitive boosting; compared with SMOTEBoost.
NT-SMOTE adds neighborhood and triangular-area sampling to SMOTE; only before/after classifier results.
Credit-risk ensemble whose SMOTE, under- and hybrid sampling are said to be 'improved' without the change described; sampling is one component, compared with models.
New decision-points-distribution and weight-assignment oversampler using SVM decisions and cluster-based generation; compared with unnamed existing algorithms.
Geometric SMOTE samples feed a Deep GMM that generates samples, both used without stated change; no comparison named.
SMOTE-NaN-DE detects noisy and borderline examples with natural neighbors and moves them by differential evolution instead of deleting; comparators not named.
An 'improved' CycleGAN, change not described, generates apple leaf disease images for ResNet; only before/after comparison.
CL-MWMOTE changes MWMOTE's internal clustering to complete linkage, a changed SMOTE-family method; compared with MWMOTE.
AD-SMOTE uses KNN average sampling density to oversample toxic comments before a bi-LSTM; compared only with existing models.
NI-MWMOTE adds adaptive noise processing and adaptive per-cluster sampling size to MWMOTE, compared with eight oversampling algorithms.
Novel over-sampling that creates synthetic texts directly in word space, one of the paper's contributions; no named comparison.
EGAHC uses entropy-guided hierarchical clustering with a dynamic neighborhood radius and fuzzy-weighted interpolation, compared with oversampling techniques.
Applies ADASYN only to complicated samples selected by decision-tree boundaries, a new way of applying an oversampler; compared with other oversampling techniques.
SHREA chains an imputation-based oversampler, random undersampling and one-class classifier bagging; compared with RBG, SBG, SBT, DTE and EUS.
NGBM identifies boundary grid cells and applies SMOTE there and undersampling elsewhere, a new allocation; no named comparison.
KNSMOTE selects safe samples whose k-means cluster class matches their label and interpolates them; compared with other oversampling algorithms.
INF-SMOTE removes noisy and overlapping borderline seeds and generates from informative minority samples; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art.
TACGAN extends ACGAN with two new generator losses for tabular data, with KNN undersampling; no comparison named.
New over-, under- and hybrid sampling that generates feature values from class-density intervals; no named comparison.
Modified back-propagation that searches the over-sampling rate during NN training, a search for how much to oversample; compared with SMOTE.
DASS selects interpolation neighbors by local density estimates, a new adaptive oversampler; compared with baseline resampling methods.
The 'enhanced SMOTE' is OVA/OVO binarization then standard SMOTE per subset on MapReduce with random forest, standard parts; compared with unnamed other methods.
EVOS combines evolutionary feature selection with an unspecified 'effective oversampling' generator for streams; the abstract does not let one tell whether the sampler is new.
NS-PPO generates with NCL plus SMOTE, then a newly designed PPO-based undersampler selects synthetic samples, a new resampling step; compared with LTRUS and other methods.
DOS-GNN's novelty is dual-feature aggregation; oversampling of fraud nodes in the learned embeddings is not described as new; compared only with GNN models.
ApRO-SyM is a synthetic minority sampler whose neighbor sets are chosen by the new Apis random movement optimizer; compared only with baseline models.
DOS-GAN trains one global GAN by taking turns over nodes' same-class data without sharing it, read as a stated training change; compared with traditional method combinations.
SMOTE-RSB* adds an editing step based on rough-set lower approximation, a cleaner of the paper's own after SMOTE; no comparison named.
MFGAN changes conditional WGAN-GP by feeding fault labels into the generator noise and adding an auxiliary classifier head; compared with SMOTE and CWGAN-GP.
Standard DCGAN generates crash cases from data reshaped to 2-D matrices; no change to the generator, compared with SMOTE and random undersampling.
Sample weights from an improved cost-sensitive C4.5 select boundary minority seeds for SMOTE and central majority for undersampling, a new selection rule; no comparison named.
FW-SMOTE uses feature importance to direct SMOTE generation, compared with regular SMOTE.
SMOTE 'improved' only by cycling over minority samples until classes are equal, a standard full-balancing use, inside an ANN fault-diagnosis method; no resampling comparison.
AWO-IHU couples adaptive weighted boundary oversampling with instance-hardness undersampling in a coordinated design; compared with SMOTE, RUS and hybrid methods.
Graph oversampling that synthesizes nodes in a learned embedding with a jointly trained edge generator and mixed in-between nodes; no named comparison.
Proposes a new bag simulation oversampling for multiple instance learning on radiomics; only with/without and other MIL classifiers compared.
TranSMOTE applies SMOTE interpolation to patch tokens of a ViT autoencoder, an existing sampler in a learned space; comparators are unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
Authors' own ASSOM-based subspace oversampler, with the generation algorithm given; compared with unnamed state-of-the-art methods.
TWAO uses commit time as a weighting factor for oversampling, compared with 8 oversampling methods.
DSO generates minority samples by minority density with noise penalties, a new oversampler; no comparison named.
UTP-DO conditions a latent diffusion model on predictive uncertainty and adds topology regularization; compared with SMOTE variants and GAN augmentation.
